title: Rounds of Hat Swapping
statement: $10$ people throw their hats into a pile. Each round, everyone still present grabs a uniformly random hat from the pile (a random permutation of the remaining hats). Everyone who got their own hat leaves with it; everyone else throws their hat back. What is the expected number of rounds until everyone has left?
insight: Each round removes 1 person on average (expected fixed points = 1), so X_t + t is a martingale and the expected stopping time equals the starting count.
redHerring: Writing a recursion over the number of people remaining, which needs the full derangement distribution.
hints: How many people leave in one round, on average, whatever the number present?
Let $X_t$ be the number present after $t$ rounds. What is $E[X_{t+1}\mid X_t]$ when $X_t>0$?
Look for a quantity combining $X_t$ and $t$ whose expected value never changes.
solution:
With $m\ge1$ people present, the expected number who get their own hat is exactly $1$, whatever $m$ is. So $M_t = X_t + t$ is a martingale until everyone has left.

At the stopping time $T$, $X_T = 0$. By optional stopping, $E[T] = E[M_T] = M_0 = 10$.
